# bitget-agent-sdk

Official Bitget foundation TypeScript SDK. Provides 109 UTA v3 operation definitions and 16 Intent verbs with full JSON Schema, an HMAC-signed REST client, client-side rate limiting, and a built-in Mock Server. The underlying library powering bitget-agent-cli and bitget-agent-mcp. For developers building quant strategies, custom MCP servers, or LLM tool-use pipelines.

## Installation
npm install @bitget-ai/bitget-agent-sdk

## Key facts
- 109 UTA v3 operations, 16 curated Intent verbs (market, order, position, account_overview, transfer_funds, etc.) mountable into any LLM framework with buildTools(); plus discover and raw meta tools always present
- safeInvoke() always resolves to { ok, ... } — never throws; all errors are typed subclasses (BitgetApiError, RateLimitError, ConfigError, etc.) for programmatic recovery
- Built-in MockServer from @bitget-ai/bitget-agent-sdk/testing for integration tests with no real API key; also runnable as standalone process with npx bitget-mock-server --port 9876
- readOnly and paperTrading safety modes; high-risk operations return { confirmationRequired: true } until confirm is passed — prevents accidental destructive calls on the first agent turn
- ESM-only (Node.js >= 20, TypeScript NodeNext resolution); zero runtime dependencies; types ship in the package

## FAQ

Q: What is bitget-agent-sdk?
A: bitget-agent-sdk is the official Bitget foundation TypeScript SDK — generated end-to-end from the UTA (v3) OpenAPI spec, covering 109 operations, with signing, rate limiting, and a mock server built in. Both bitget-agent-cli and bitget-agent-mcp are built on top of it, making it the foundational layer of the entire Bitget Agent Hub ecosystem.

Q: What developer use cases is this SDK designed for?
A: Building quantitative trading strategies, custom MCP servers, LLM tool-use pipelines, automated trading bots, and any TypeScript or JavaScript project that needs programmatic access to Bitget's UTA API.

Q: How is this different from calling the Bitget REST API directly?
A: The SDK handles HMAC-SHA256 request signing, client-side rate limiting, and typed error classes. It provides 16 curated Intent verbs plus the full 1:1 operation surface, all mountable into any LLM tool-use framework. safeInvoke gives every call a uniform { ok, ... } shape — no need to wrap each handler in try/catch yourself.

Q: How do I test without hitting live endpoints?
A: Import MockServer from the @bitget-ai/bitget-agent-sdk/testing subpath. It provides an in-memory Bitget API simulator for integration tests with no real API key needed. Alternatively, run npx bitget-mock-server --port 9876 as a standalone process.

Q: Does this SDK support CommonJS?
A: No, it is ESM-only ("type": "module"). Requires Node.js >= 20 and NodeNext module resolution.

Q: How do I load only specific modules?
A: Use loadConfig({ modules: ["account", "trade"] }) to load a named subset, or loadConfig({ modules: "all" }) to load all visible modules. broker and instloan are hidden modules and must be named explicitly.

Q: I'm on a classic Bitget account — can I use this?
A: Yes, but classic accounts need to create an Agent sub-account first via the API, then use that sub-account's API key for MCP / CLI / Skill tools.

Q: Is it officially from Bitget and free to use?
A: Yes. It is an official open-source SDK published by Bitget under the MIT license, free to use.
